purpose: Short original explanations for terms exposed by the collection companion. Stable definitions point to canonical collection or pinned knowledge resources; changeable game mechanics point to the reviewed mechanics registry.

entries.definition: A percentage summary of the three appraisal IVs. Exact Attack, Defense, and HP IVs carry the underlying values.
entries.why_it_matters: Two Pokémon can share the same IV percentage while distributing those IVs differently, which can change league eligibility or matchup behavior.

entries.definition: The individual Attack, Defense, and HP appraisal values, each recorded from 0 through 15 when the source export provides them.
entries.why_it_matters: Exact values support hundo/nundo detection, CP calculations, and PvP IV comparisons that a single percentage cannot express.

entries.definition: Pokémon GO appraisal bands derived from the appraisal IV total. They summarize ordinary IV quality and do not encode PvP rank.
entries.why_it_matters: A lower-star Pokémon can have a stronger league-capped PvP IV spread than a higher-star copy.

entries.definition: A Pokémon whose Attack, Defense, and HP IVs are all 15.
entries.why_it_matters: It is the maximum ordinary IV combination, while specific league-capped PvP formats can prefer different distributions.

entries.definition: A Pokémon whose Attack, Defense, and HP IVs are all 0.
entries.why_it_matters: It is a rare collector pattern and should remain distinguishable from ordinary low-IV transfer candidates.

entries.definition: A ranking of an IV combination under a specified league CP cap and evolution target. The repository treats Poke Genie rank as an IV-ranking input rather than a current-meta ranking.
entries.why_it_matters: Rank 1 describes one IV optimization target; matchups, moves, team role, cup rules, and current meta can change which owned copy performs best.

entries.definition: A combined measure of battle Attack, Defense, and HP commonly used to compare league-capped IV combinations.
entries.why_it_matters: It summarizes overall stat volume and does not by itself predict every matchup or breakpoint.

entries.definition: The maximum CP allowed by a league or cup format when that format defines one.
entries.why_it_matters: Powering past a cap can make a Pokémon ineligible for that format.

entries.definition: The tie-resolution concept used when opposing Charged Attacks are launched together. The battle model must use comparable battle Attack rather than Attack IV alone.
entries.why_it_matters: A higher Attack IV does not automatically prove CMP advantage because level, base stats, and other modifiers contribute to battle Attack.

entries.definition: A threshold where a stat change alters discrete damage in a modeled matchup.
entries.why_it_matters: A small Attack difference can matter when it crosses a specific matchup threshold even if another copy has higher overall stat product.

entries.definition: A threshold where additional defensive bulk changes discrete incoming damage in a modeled matchup.
entries.why_it_matters: Bulkpoints are matchup-specific and require an explicit battle model and opponent assumptions.

entries.definition: Damage dealt per unit of time under a stated battle model.
entries.why_it_matters: Higher DPS can shorten battles, while survivability and total damage can still change the best team choice.

entries.definition: Total modeled damage a Pokémon deals before fainting or otherwise leaving the modeled battle.
entries.why_it_matters: TDO emphasizes sustained contribution and can favor bulkier options than a DPS-only ranking.

entries.definition: Modeled time required for the selected attackers and assumptions to defeat a target.
entries.why_it_matters: TTW depends on the chosen boss, moves, weather or friendship assumptions, team composition, and model version.

entries.definition: How long an attacker or defender remains effective under a stated battle model.
entries.why_it_matters: A Pokémon with lower peak damage can contribute more total value when it stays active longer.

entries.definition: Battle modifiers associated with Shadow Pokémon. The exact supported rules come from the reviewed mechanics registry.
entries.why_it_matters: Shadow status changes battle tradeoffs and can make purification an irreversible decision that deserves separate review.

entries.definition: The in-game action that changes a Shadow Pokémon into a Purified Pokémon under the current reviewed mechanics.
entries.why_it_matters: The action is irreversible, changes relevant stats or moves under current rules, and should be reviewed before use.

entries.definition: A Shadow-associated Charged Attack whose removal rules can depend on current Pokémon GO mechanics or events.
entries.why_it_matters: Move availability can block an otherwise attractive build, so current removal rules must be checked before spending resources.

entries.definition: A Charged Attack associated with Purified Pokémon under the reviewed mechanics.
entries.why_it_matters: Purification can alter move options, so a build comparison should account for the resulting moveset rather than IV changes alone.

entries.definition: The repeatedly used attack that generates energy in battle systems where the model supports that mechanic.
entries.why_it_matters: Fast Move damage, energy generation, typing, and timing shape how quickly Charged Moves become available.

entries.definition: An attack that consumes accumulated battle energy where the applicable battle system uses that mechanic.
entries.why_it_matters: Move choice changes coverage, shield pressure, damage windows, and whether an owned Pokémon needs a TM or second move.

entries.definition: A move whose ordinary availability is restricted relative to the current standard move pool.
entries.why_it_matters: A recommended build can be blocked or require an Elite TM when the needed move is unavailable through ordinary TMs.

entries.definition: A scarce item used to select moves from a broader eligible pool under current Pokémon GO rules.
entries.why_it_matters: Its scarcity creates an opportunity cost, so plans should compare owned alternatives before recommending its use.

entries.definition: Progression associated with repeated Mega Evolution under the reviewed current mechanics.
entries.why_it_matters: Mega-related bonuses and planning depend on the current mechanic state and the specific owned Pokémon.

entries.definition: A current Mega-related progression concept tracked only when the reviewed mechanics registry supports it.
entries.why_it_matters: Current benefits can change, so recommendations should use the reviewed mechanic version rather than static prose.

entries.definition: A transformation category represented in the pinned knowledge and reviewed current mechanics where supported.
entries.why_it_matters: Eligibility is stable knowledge, while current costs, bonuses, and availability can require fresh mechanic data.

entries.definition: A Pokémon GO Max-system state or eligibility tracked from versioned knowledge and reviewed mechanics.
entries.why_it_matters: Max Battle recommendations require the exact owned record plus current supported Max mechanics.

entries.definition: A distinct Max-system form or capability tracked separately from ordinary Dynamax where supported.
entries.why_it_matters: Gigantamax eligibility and move behavior can differ from ordinary Dynamax and should remain explicitly identified.

entries.definition: Max Battle move categories whose exact effects and upgrade rules come from the reviewed mechanics registry.
entries.why_it_matters: Resource planning depends on which Max move is being improved and the current cost/effect rules.

entries.definition: A Max-system resource tracked by the Resource Vault when the user enters a balance.
entries.why_it_matters: Plans should reserve entered balances across competing Max investments instead of silently spending the same resource twice.

entries.definition: A reviewed current mechanic that can change effective IV-related outcomes under supported conditions.
entries.why_it_matters: Eligibility, item expiration, and resulting build value must be evaluated from the current mechanic contract before committing a scarce item.

entries.definition: A scarce Hyper Training item tracked with optional local balance and expiration information when applicable.
entries.why_it_matters: Its scarcity and possible time limit make accidental or low-value spending costly.

entries.definition: A current mechanic combining supported Pokémon into a fused state under reviewed rules.
entries.why_it_matters: Fusion can affect trade, transfer, move, and resource decisions, so exact state and current rules must be confirmed.

entries.definition: Field effects activated by specific supported moves under reviewed current Pokémon GO mechanics.
entries.why_it_matters: Activation costs, duration, stacking, and supported moves can change the value of a resource plan.

entries.definition: The repository classification describing where a claim comes from, such as canonical collection data, official current mechanics, reviewed community data, or a calculation.
entries.why_it_matters: Authority labels help distinguish direct source facts from model outputs and local assumptions.

entries.definition: Whether time-sensitive data remains inside its declared age and validity window at the time it is used.
entries.why_it_matters: Rotating events, raids, PvP formats, Rocket lineups, and other current claims should stop driving recommendations after their freshness window expires.

entries.definition: A deterministic model output produced from explicit inputs, assumptions, and a versioned implementation.
entries.why_it_matters: Simulation results depend on the model and inputs and should remain distinguishable from direct game-source facts.

entries.definition: A state used when the repository lacks enough supported information to make a stronger claim.
entries.why_it_matters: Unknown collector, mechanic, cost, or freshness data should block destructive or expensive conclusions that depend on it.

entries.definition: The repository's exact normalized identity for one owned Pokémon record from the canonical collection.
entries.why_it_matters: Recommendations and handoffs can point back to the specific owned Pokémon instead of relying on species-level guesses.

entries.definition: The completeness and recency of fields supplied by the collection export for an owned record.
entries.why_it_matters: Missing or stale scan fields can make a recommendation less reliable and can trigger a rescan request before spending resources.

entries.definition: The conservative process for deciding whether repeated imported rows represent the same owned Pokémon or distinct copies.
entries.why_it_matters: Incorrect reconciliation can lose collection history or collapse distinct Pokémon, so ambiguous cases require explicit review.
